title: Which bracket expressions match seventy three minus fourteen?
description: Two expressions are matched with four options that have brackets, by opening each bracket using the sign before it. The matches are checked by working out the values.
teaching_notes: Let the child try first, then compare. One idea: open each bracket by looking at the sign before it, then compare the terms. Ask the child to check each match by working out the value.

video_script.why: The child opens each bracket using the sign before it and matches the terms, as in the coins example with a bracket after a plus sign.
video_script.substitution: The same method works with other numbers: open each bracket and compare the terms.
video_script.anchor: two expressions at the top and four options with brackets in a row below
video_script.payoff_line: Expressions with the same terms have the same value.

final_answer.spoken: the first expression equals the second and third options, and the second expression equals the first and fourth options

maths_rules: 73 - (14 - 1) = 73 - 14 + 1: the minus before the bracket flips the signs inside
73 + (-14 + 1) = 73 - 14 + 1: the plus before the bracket keeps the signs inside
73 - (14 + 1) = 73 - 14 - 1: the minus before the bracket flips the signs inside
73 + (-14 - 1) = 73 - 14 - 1: the plus before the bracket keeps the signs inside
video_script.design: One idea: open each bracket by the sign before it, then compare the terms. The expressions and options stay in the anchor band; the working band shows each opening. No hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, look at the first expression, seventy three minus fourteen plus one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seventy three minus the bracket fourteen minus one has the minus sign before the bracket.
The signs inside flip, giving seventy three minus fourteen plus one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Seventy three plus the bracket minus fourteen plus one has the plus sign before it.
The signs inside stay, giving seventy three minus fourteen plus one.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Both match the first expression.

marks.m1: 73 − 14 − 1 is written with its terms boxed
marks.m2: 73 − (14 + 1) is opened with the signs flipped: 73 − 14 − 1
marks.m3: 73 + (−14 − 1) is opened with the signs kept: 73 − 14 − 1
marks.m4: the two openings are ticked as matches

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, look at the second expression, seventy three minus fourteen minus one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seventy three minus the bracket fourteen plus one flips to seventy three minus fourteen minus one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Seventy three plus the bracket minus fourteen minus one keeps its signs, and gives the same.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Both match the second expression.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, check by values.
Seventy three minus fourteen plus one is sixty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seventy three minus the bracket fourteen minus one is seventy three minus thirteen, which is sixty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Seventy three minus fourteen minus one is fifty eight.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Seventy three minus the bracket fourteen plus one is seventy three minus fifteen, also fifty eight.

marks.m2: the first expression is joined to the second and third options
marks.m3: the second expression is joined to the first and fourth options
